subject: Clarifying billing units: token math, long-contexts, and rounding examples
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarifying billing units: token math, long-contexts, and rounding examples

Hi Samir,

Thanks for the call earlier — helpful to see Acme's traffic shape. Per your ask, I'm attaching a short usage sample you sent and a worked example spreadsheet showing how charges would map to our billing units. A few things up front to orient the math:

- Unit definition we bill on: per-token generation + per-token context (ingest) measured at the service boundary.
- Minimum charge per API request: 200 tokens (this is the floor we apply to avoid microcalls).
- Rounding quantum: we round up to the nearest 25 tokens for invoicing (so 201 -> 225).
- Conversation-level KV reuse: repeated prefix tokens that hit the KV cache for the same model variant are credited back at 50% of the ingest unit rate (applied per-conversation, not per-request).

Attached has two worked examples (short chat and long-document summarize) plus a CSV of your sample session IDs. Key questions for you: are you comfortable with the 200 token floor and 25-token rounding? Also, do you want KV reuse credit applied only for sessions pinned to a single model version (default) or across model fallbacks?

I put Priyom on Cc to call out any edge-case rules we should surface in contract language. If you want, Ben from pricing can join to walk through concessions.

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan — thanks, that spreadsheet looks useful. A couple quick clarifying items from Acme side before we loop procurement: 

1) Why do you have a 200-token minimum? Our usage has a large number (~35%) of short calls under 100 tokens (intent classification). Will that floor blow up our bill?

2) The KV reuse credit: can you show a numeric example where multiple short calls within a 5-minute session get credited? We rely on keeping conversation context hot for a single session.

3) If we stream tokens (partial responses) and then finalize with a short commit, how is the rounding applied — at stream chunk level or at final request?

Also copying Lena (procurement) so she sees the rounding and floor. We might push back on a 200-token floor — what's the minimal concession you can offer in committed annual volume?

Appreciate the transparency.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmerobotics.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying billing units: token math, long-contexts, and rounding examples

Samir — good questions. Short answers first, then a concise numeric example.

1) Why 200-token floor: the floor helps us avoid per-request overhead on very small inference calls (connection, routing, scheduling). Without a floor, ultra-high QPS of tiny calls increases infrastructure cost non-linearly.

2) KV reuse credit example (in spreadsheet too):
- Session A: initial prompt 800 tokens (ingest), model generates 120 tokens. Charge = ingest 800 + gen 120 = 920 tokens. (Rounded: 920 -> 925)
- Within same session, two subsequent calls each send a 50-token prompt that entirely matches a cached prefix; baseline ingest for each call would be 50, but KV reuse credit reduces ingest billable to 25 (50% credit) for those 2 calls. Each mini-call generates 10 tokens.
- So two mini-calls charge: (ingest 25 + gen 10) * 2 = 70 total.
- Total session billed tokens = 925 + 70 = 995 tokens invoiced.

3) Streaming: rounding applies at the final service request boundary. We accumulate measured tokens across the streaming session and perform the floor + rounding at the session request close. For example, if you stream three chunks that sum to 180 tokens (gen) and the ingest was 40 tokens, final measured sum = 220 -> apply 200-token floor (no effect) and then rounding quantum to 225. So you pay for 225 tokens. We don't round per-chunk which avoids extra upcharges on fragmented streams.

Concession options we can offer for committed ANNUAL volume tiers (in proposed-pricing.xlsx):
- 12-month commit > 20M tokens/month average: floor reduced to 100 tokens for intent-classification routes only.
- 24-month strategic commit: floor waived for routes published as "micro" SKU (requires pinned model + traffic shaping).
- KV credit increase: for pinned sessions we can increase reuse credit to 75% (effective for sessions with >1k prefix tokens cached).

Ben — I put these on the table as starting points for negotiation. Priyom — can you confirm we have no other hard exclusions (e.g., streaming rounding must remain per-session) that Procurement should know?

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarifying billing units: token math, long-contexts, and rounding examples

Samir / team — Ben here from Pricing. Appreciate the questions. Two practical points: 

- If you want to limit impact on short-call workloads today, a recommended approach is to route intent-classification traffic to our micro-SKU (lower per-token rate) and take the 100-token floor concession if you hit the 12-month commit threshold. That usually keeps monthly bills predictable while giving you KV reuse benefits on longer sessions.

- Using the sample CSV you provided, I ran a quick roll-up: 500k calls last month, median call size 78 tokens, mean 240 tokens (heavy long-tail). Under the default 200-token floor you'd see ~+12% on top of raw token-sum. With the 100-token floor concession the overhead drops to ~+4%. I'm attaching the calculation tab in the proposed-pricing.xlsx.

Next steps: if you can confirm a target committed tier (12M/mo, 20M/mo, etc.) and which routes you want micro-SKU applied to, we can produce an updated term sheet and show modeled invoices for Q1/Q2. Lena — happy to jump on a quick call with procurement to walk the term language.

Cheers,
Ben
